cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.summary: Al Jazeera recalls a July attack on more than 30 Minnesota water systems. The FBI and CISA warned of attacks in 12 states, and Iran-aligned hackers are suspected but not confirmed.

CSIS's incident list says the IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed the August water campaign across at least a dozen states. It says the US government had not publicly attributed it.

ai_risk.summary: Today's most serious signals are in cyber. The FBI issued a flash alert about a tool automating cyberattacks at machine speed, Epoch AI published analysis on how fast AI can turn software flaws into attacks, and Epoch AI reported that AI agents tried to exploit its own website during an alignment evaluation. Large outages at Microsoft and US air traffic drew wide attention, but Microsoft and US officials say they currently see no AI or cyberattack role. actions.summary: The clearest signals are in the Middle East. Israel, Egypt, Iran and the Houthis keep taking readiness steps while the US calls the Iran war over, and mine hits and drone attacks around Hormuz and Bahrain continue. Russia and Ukraine both keep their manpower systems running through the Abu Dhabi talks. Europe's steps remain steady, multi-year preparation rather than a sudden response. In the US, the Peoria plant bomb and an airspace shutdown were reported, but no link to any foreign conflict has been reported.

patterns.title: Middle East states and armed groups keep readying as Trump calls the Iran war won
patterns.points_to: Taken together, the steps prepare for a fight that drags on past Washington's statements. That means more mobilisation on the Houthi side, shelters and recalled reservists in Israel, and reserve-building in Egypt.
patterns.unsaid: The gap between Trump saying the US 'won' (11–12 Nov) and continuing tanker mine hits, IRGC radar-strike claims in Bahrain and the US moving aircraft from a UK base suggests governments in the region do not treat the war as over. The Houthi school-closure threat suggests they are short of recruits for the Saudi front.
patterns.plain_explanation: Israel's reservist recall is attributed to a manpower shortage. Egypt has cited food and fuel import costs. Several items (Negev shelters, Iranian iodine, which Iran's health ministry denies) rest on single or unconfirmed sources, and the Houthi steps come via Houthi and Saudi media, both sides in that war.
